lines.text: That night the dream is different. A desk, a candle, a woman bent over her work, papers weighted with a knife. Her sleeves are rolled, and up her forearm run etchings like his.
She writes fast, checks one page against another, writes again. Working. Urgent. Then she stops mid line and looks up. At him.
You can see me. Good. Don't talk. Look.
Her eyes go to the wall behind her. Stone, one narrow window, a heavy door with the hinges on the outside. Then the candle gutters, and the dream is gone.
Sophia is going to want every word of that written down.
